data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A budget-exhausted run can be safely resumed if and only if three conditions hold jointly: (1) the halt was event-boundary-aligned\u2014budget exhaustion was checked between event commits, never mid-write, so no partial event exists in the log; (2) the append-only identity chain (e.g., hash chain linking each event to its predecessor) is intact and verifiable up to the last committed event; (3) the full causal state needed for continuation is reconstructable from the committed event sequence alone. Resumption must be refused when any of these fails: a partial write exists (crash or mid-write budget exhaustion), the chain is broken or unverifiable, or state reconstruction is incomplete because an in-flight operation left uncommitted state.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the budget checker can trigger mid-write (e.g., streaming token generation stops partway through an event body before the commit), then budget exhaustion itself can create a partial write, and the clean-halt assumption fails even for budget-caused halts.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the storage layer does not guarantee atomicity of append operations, a crash during persist could leave a partially written event even if the budget check was event-boundary-aligned.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system maintains state outside the event log (e.g., in-memory caches, external database cursors) that is not reconstructable from replay, condition (3) fails and resumption would silently diverge.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the identity scheme allows the partial event to be syntactically valid but semantically incomplete (e.g., the hash covers only the event header, not the body), verification could pass on a corrupt entry.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The budget checker evaluates remaining tokens only at event-commit boundaries (after a full event is persisted and its identity hash linked). When the check fails, the system writes a terminal 'halt' event marking the resumption point and stops. On resumption, the system re-reads the log, verifies the hash chain from genesis to the halt event, reconstructs working state via replay, and continues appending from the verified tail. A partial write would manifest as a trailing event whose hash does not link to its predecessor or whose content is truncated\u2014this is detectable on verification and triggers refusal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
